rationale: The Court will reverse the Eighth Circuit and hold that Title VII does not require a freestanding “materially significant disadvantage” showing; a plaintiff must show a nontrivial, objectively identifiable discriminatory change in the terms or conditions of employment, even without pay or rank loss. A lone Alito dissent is likely to press administrability and argue for a more demanding, objective harm screen to avoid turning Title VII into a super-personnel code.
